title: "Nonnegative Matrix Factorization"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Overview

This example demonstrates nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) on a 5x4 data
matrix. NMF finds two nonnegative matrices `W` and `H`
whose product approximates the nonnegative input matrix `A`, i.e. `A ~= W H`.

```{r library}
library(aoclda)
```

## Define Data

```{r data}
a <- matrix(
  c(
    1., 2., 3., 4.,
    2., 4., 6., 8.,
    3., 6., 9., 12.,
    4., 1., 5., 2.,
    5., 3., 8., 4.
  ),
  nrow = 5, ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE
)
```

## Fit and Transform

Fit the model using NNDSVDa initialization and obtain the left factor `W`.

```{r nmf}
nmf <- NMF$new(n_components = 2, solver = "mu", beta_loss = "frobenius",
               max_iter = 200, tol = 1.0e-6, init = "nndsvda")
w <- nmf$fit_transform(a)
h <- nmf$h
```

## Results

```{r results}
cat("W:\n")
print(w)

cat("\nH:\n")
print(h)

cat("\nReconstruction error:", nmf$reconstruction_err, "\n")
cat("Iterations performed:", nmf$n_iter, "\n")
```

## Transform New Samples

Transform two new samples into the component space, then reconstruct them in the
original feature space.

```{r transform}
a_new <- matrix(
  c(
    2., 3., 5., 4.,
    1., 1., 2., 1.
  ),
  nrow = 2, ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE
)

w_new <- nmf$transform(a_new)
a_rec <- nmf$inverse_transform(w_new)

cat("W_new = transform(A_new):\n")
print(w_new)

cat("\ninverse_transform(W_new) ~= A_new:\n")
print(a_rec)
```
